questions.prompt: TP=18, FP=2, FN=12, TN=968. Compute recall. (decimal, tolerance 0.001)
Precision 0.5 and recall 1.0. What is F1? (decimal, tolerance 0.001)
questions.explanation: 2·0.5·1/1.5=0.667. The harmonic mean punishes the weaker value.

questions.prompt: A false alarm costs 2 and a miss costs 18. Calibrated probability threshold for predicting positive? (decimal, tolerance 0.001)
On a test set FP=12 and FN=7 with c_FP=1 and c_FN=5. What is the total cost? (integer, tolerance 0.01)
Sensitivity 0.95, specificity 0.98, prevalence 2%. What is the precision? (decimal, tolerance 0.002)
Bins: 6 predictions at 0.7 with 5 positives, and 4 predictions at 0.2 with 0 positives. What is the ECE? (decimal, tolerance 0.001)
Calibrated at balanced prior, p=0.5 for a case. Deployment prevalence is 20%. What is the prior-corrected probability? (decimal, tolerance 0.002)
A robot team reports 97% accuracy for a rare-event detector (1% positive). Which follow-up is most informative?
options: Ask for recall, precision, and the accuracy of always predicting negative.
Ask for the training loss, which shows how well the model fitted the data.
Ask for the number of epochs, which shows how long the model was trained.
Ask whether accuracy was computed in float64, which affects its exact value.
questions.explanation: Only per-class metrics and a baseline show whether 97% is meaningful when 99% is free.

questions.prompt: A model ranks positives above negatives perfectly (AUC=1) but outputs 0.99 for every example. Which statement is true?
options: It is badly calibrated: ECE is large although ranking is perfect.
It is well calibrated because AUC is 1 and the ranking is perfect.
Calibration is undefined for such a model, since all the outputs are equal.
Precision must be 1, because the model ranks every positive above every negative.
questions.explanation: AUC measures ordering only; confidence 0.99 is wrong for negatives.

questions.prompt: You select the threshold maximizing F1 on the test set and report that F1. Which fix is correct?
options: Use a lower threshold so that recall is higher and the F1 stays the same.
Report the F1 at the best threshold but add the word 'tuned' to the table.
Choose it on the training set, which is larger and gives a more stable estimate.
Choose the threshold on a validation split and report once on the untouched test set.
questions.explanation: Anything optimized on a dataset biases the score on that dataset.

questions.prompt: Fifty useless models each have validation accuracy ~N(0.5, 0.05²). Approximate the expected best score using μ+σ·sqrt(2 ln K). (decimal, tolerance 0.01)
questions.explanation: sqrt(2 ln 50)=2.80, so 0.5+0.14=0.64 (a rough upper estimate; exact order statistic is about 0.61).
